lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The Experience section should place Harbor Payments between Coastal Marine Services and Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The current order places a 2024 internship below a role that ended in 2023, which looks accidental.

items.says: A product-focused version should foreground the internship and app project or use clearly labeled product-relevant and additional-experience sections.
items.because: Those experiences are more directly relevant to product roles than the mechanic role.

items.says: Remove “USA” from all locations if every role is domestic and space is tight.
Use en dashes consistently in date ranges.
Choose one convention for numbers under 10 and apply it consistently.
Keep bullets to roughly two lines where possible.
Keep the résumé to one page if possible by removing duplicate and low-impact bullets.
Verify every metric’s scope, time period, and whether it was measured, estimated, or projected.
The mechanic entry should make transferable themes such as reliability, prioritization, compliance, and uptime clearer.
items.because: The role should not occupy more attention than directly relevant product experience.

items.says: Replace the placeholder phone number, email address, and LinkedIn URL before submitting.
items.because: Recruiters commonly cross-check profiles, and inconsistencies can undermine otherwise strong experience.

items.says: Make the LinkedIn URL clickable in the PDF.
Confirm that the LinkedIn profile matches the résumé’s dates, titles, and metrics.
items.because: Recruiters commonly cross-check profiles, and inconsistencies can undermine otherwise strong experience.

items.says: Make the MBA’s completion status unmistakable if the degree was awarded.
items.because: Since June 2025 has passed, readers should not have to wonder whether the degree was awarded or merely expected.

items.says: Clarify whether all 14 vessels were serviced by you, your team, or the broader company.
items.because: The scope and your individual contribution are not fully clear.

items.says: Clarify whether the sub-five-day dry-dock time was a target, average, or maximum.
items.because: The metric’s scope is not fully clear.

items.says: Add a baseline or comparison for the dry-dock metric if available.
Add scale, inspection results, uptime improvement, avoided failures, or a compliance outcome, or cut the bullet for product applications.
items.because: It currently reads as a routine responsibility rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Replace the vague statement that the meeting discussed scorecards with the decisions or actions the scorecards enabled.
items.because: Discussion alone is not an outcome.

items.says: Add carrier count, region size, service improvement, cost reduction, or an escalation outcome.
items.because: The bullet lacks a concrete result or scale.

items.says: Remove the meeting-management detail if it did not create a distinct result.
items.because: Discussion alone is not an outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% reduction in pick errors is relative.
Add the period over which the pick-error reduction was measured.
Consider shortening “12 consecutive quarters” if space is tight.
items.because: The date range already demonstrates tenure.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was calculated if the metric could be challenged.
Use consistent punctuation in “sales, finance, and operations.”
Break apart or reduce the software rollout, procedure revision, driver training, vendor negotiation, and time-savings initiatives in one bullet.
items.because: The bullet is overloaded, making the central accomplishment harder to identify.

items.says: Make the connection between the work and the 1,800 saved hours explicit.
items.because: The current causal claim is hard to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 saved hours were measured after implementation or estimated.
items.because: The current causal claim is hard to assess.

items.says: Present any separate financial result from the telematics negotiation distinctly rather than burying it.
items.because: Too many initiatives are attributed to one bullet.

items.says: Clarify that the single verification step removed redundancy without weakening compliance or fraud controls.
items.because: The wording could suggest that a compliance step was simply removed.

items.says: Clarify whether 2,300 merchants completed the pilot or were merely eligible for it.
State whether the onboarding result was statistically or operationally validated if possible.
Characterize the conversion change as a five-percentage-point increase rather than a 5% increase.
Add the test period or confidence threshold if important and supportable.
Clarify what “all merchants” means geographically or operationally.
Reassess whether support tickets closed correctly represented Reach in the RICE framework.
items.because: Reach normally reflects affected users, accounts, transactions, cases, or another unit, while ticket reduction may belong under expected impact.

items.says: Define the period and unit used for Reach, or remove the framework name if it was not applied rigorously.
items.because: A questionable definition may make product reviewers doubt your command of RICE.

items.says: Add an explicit subject so ownership is grammatically clear.
items.because: The current construction obscures ownership.

items.says: Specify what roadmap priority or decision resulted.
items.because: The bullet ends with a vague result.

items.says: Add the expected or realized business impact of the roadmap decision.
items.because: The bullet is process-heavy.

items.says: Consider consolidating this bullet with the preceding RICE bullet.
items.because: Both appear to describe the same roadmap decision.

items.says: This checkout-testing bullet duplicates the earlier checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: The repetition weakens one of the résumé’s strongest product accomplishments.

items.says: The session-randomized test should not be reported as a causal effect on individual customers without accounting for users appearing in both variants.
items.because: Session-level randomization supports a session-level conclusion, not necessarily a customer-level conclusion.

items.says: Check repeat-user contamination and independence assumptions.
items.because: Users may have appeared in both variants.

items.says: Clarify whether the two-region rollout was funded, launched, or completed.
items.because: These represent different levels of impact.

items.says: Use rollout results instead of approval alone if later results are available.
items.because: Implementation impact is stronger and more precise than approval.

items.says: Clarify whether the project is an active student venture, registered organization, or independent project.
items.because: The project’s current status and organizational scope should be accurate.

items.says: Add team size if it demonstrates leadership.
Update “Present” if the project ended when you graduated.
items.because: The project’s current status should be accurate.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 means registered users, eligible students, reached students, or active users.
items.because: The adoption metric is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain how the nine tonnes were measured or estimated if space allows.
Ensure that “first year” corresponds cleanly to the project dates.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: A math error is damaging, especially for analytics-heavy product roles.

items.says: Define the behavior that counts as a weekly active user.
Do not attribute the full user increase to reminders without an experiment, controlled cohort comparison, or suitable before-and-after evidence.
items.because: Interviews choosing the feature do not by themselves establish causality.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 26.7%, and percentage-point accuracy matters.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period for the fill-rate increase.
Explain whether the volunteer shift system increased supply, reduced missed pickups, or improved operational coverage.
items.because: The mechanism is currently unclear.

items.says: Use the standard plural “savings” for recurring cost reductions.
Clarify whether the $2.4M amount was modeled by the team, validated by the client, or realized.
items.because: Estimated savings should not be mistaken for realized savings.

items.says: Briefly indicate the main basis of the $2.4M estimate if available.
Replace the passive construction with wording that makes your role and the team’s ownership clear.
items.because: The current construction hides ownership.

items.says: Add a measurable result from shortening the form, such as intake time, completion rate, errors, workload, or patient satisfaction.
items.because: The bullet lacks an outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether adoption occurred during the practicum or was only approved.
The pilot-approval outcome overlaps with the pilot-funding outcome in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The two pilot-approval bullets are duplicative.

items.says: Clarify whether approval, funding, and launch were separate stages.
items.because: These are different levels of implementation.

items.says: Add pilot results if they became available.
items.because: Presentation alone is not the accomplishment; the enabled decision or implementation is.

items.says: Keep only product skills that can be defended with specific examples.
items.because: Skills should reinforce demonstrated evidence rather than introduce unsupported claims.

items.says: Reassess the A/B testing skill after correcting the session-level experimentation issue.
items.because: The current experiment overstates what its design supports.

items.says: Use terminology consistently between the skills section and the experience bullets.
Consider adding prioritization, experimentation design, analytics, or product discovery only when supported by the experience.
items.because: Skills should reinforce demonstrated evidence.

items.says: The tools list is thin for data-oriented product roles, particularly because SQL is absent.
items.because: SQL may be noticeable in product analytics recruiting, though it should be added only if interview-ready.

items.says: Specify the Excel capability more precisely if it is advanced enough to do so.
items.because: Subjective proficiency ratings should still be avoided.
